mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over two consecutive quarters signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 8% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% and UNRATE exceeds 8%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its previous 12-month average by more than 3% signals an acceleration in economic activity, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when INDPRO exceeds its 12-month average by more than 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 jobs combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate by at least 0.4 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month AND UNRATE +0.4pp month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during months with >100k job losses and a 0.4pp rise in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals weakening housing demand, which historically precedes negative equity market performance over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month MA by > 10% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained HOUST weakness below its 12-month MA by >10%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1% over two months signals a risk of policy overtightening, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls below 1% in the same two-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate is below 6% signals a synchronized improvement in supply and labor conditions, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when INDPRO rises by >1% and UNRATE is below 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) by more than 8% alongside a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 1% signals a shift from consumption to saving, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of >8% savings growth and >1% consumption decline.
